events.description: Israel killed senior Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr in Beirut (hosts: 'in the last week')
Ismail Haniyeh assassinated in Tehran hours after attending the inauguration of Iran's new president
Israel announced it had killed Hamas military commander Mohammed Deif; Hamas has not acknowledged
Iran's missile and drone attack on Israel; ~95% intercepted by Israel, US, UK, France, Jordan (and probably Saudis); Israel hit an air-defense site in response
Iranian IRGC general killed in Syria (Damascus), name not recalled by hosts
US killed Qasem Soleimani in Baghdad; Iran fired ballistic missiles at US forces in Iraq
Marine barracks bombing in Beirut, linked to Fuad Shukr; drove the US out of Lebanon
Hezbollah commander Musa Ali Daqduq sent to Iraq after the US invasion to help build Shia militias with Soleimani
Tower 22 attack by Iraqi militia killed three Americans, prompting a meaningful US response
Israeli strike on Hodeidah port; roughly two weeks without Houthi attacks afterwards
Wagner column ambushed in a sandstorm in northern Mali; 25-50 killed, ~15 captured; claimed by Tuareg rebels and separately by JNIM; Ukraine claimed then Tuaregs denied its involvement
Two Israeli airstrikes in the Tulkarm area of the northern West Bank
Israel Army Radio reported a plan by Tulkarm-area terrorist groups to infiltrate Israel along the seam line
Houthi commander Hussein Abdullah reportedly killed in Lebanon or Iraq, per Iranian state media
Hamas founder Ahmed Yassin killed by Israel; replacement killed a month later (hosts: 'early 2000s')
Russia took Avdiivka in spring and has retaken most of Ukraine's 2023 gains; Ukraine lowered conscription age from 27 to 25; F-16s arrived

key_claims: Iran's 'axis of resistance' (Hezbollah, Hamas, PIJ, Houthis, Iraqi militias) is increasingly intertwined, at least in media; a coordinated multi-front strike is the most dangerous scenario for Israel.
Haniyeh's killing in Tehran while a 'guest' is more severe for Iran than the IRGC general killed in Syria; the hosts compare it to Soleimani and expect retaliation, possibly on Iran's own timetable.
Killing Deif and Haniyeh is a PR win but decapitation does not destroy organizations (bin Laden, Zawahiri, Zarqawi, Baghdadi); Sinwar remains.
The West Bank is the 'ticking time bomb': maturing Hamas/PIJ networks in Tulkarm, Iranian weapons smuggling, weak PA, car bombs.
Iran builds proxy cohesion by circulating commanders (Daqduq to Iraq, Houthi commander abroad) and leverages each group's strengths.
US deterrence against Iran's proxies has eroded; the US targets Houthi weapons but not leadership and left the Iranian intelligence ship untouched.
The Wagner ambush in Mali involved Tuareg rebels likely coordinating with JNIM; Ukraine's claimed involvement risks flirting with al-Qaeda, echoing Western dalliances with HTS and the PKK/SDF.
Preston Stewart notes episodic bans on TikTok since 7 October, and earlier for discussing Taliban/Islamic State.
